A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from RACRO to RAPID, with shared authors, training data, reasoning benchmarks, and retained appendix examples. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component and reward-computation ablations, training analyses, and automated and human caption evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original RAPID experiments, including revised ablations, general vision-language evaluations, compute analyses, and human caption assessments.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming CRO to VPO, v2 adds a model-judged caption-validity penalty to the correctness reward (Equation 3). It incorporates sequential GRPO/VPO optimization into the main method and adds a GRPO recovery stage for the 3B model. GRPO combinations already appeared in v1, but its main results used CRO alone.

E1.justification: ViRL39K and the seven main reasoning benchmarks remain. v2 adds general vision-language evaluations on MME, MMBench-v1.1, MM-Vet, SEED-Image, MMStar, RealWorld-QA, MMT-Bench, and BLINK, extending coverage to general recognition, OCR, and perception tasks. These evaluations test the optimized perception model with the external reasoner disabled.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparators including ECSO, OmniCaptioner, ReVisual-R1, Gemma-3, and Ovis2, while removing VisualPRM best-of-eight comparisons and several earlier rows, including o1 and OpenVLThinker. Appendix D adds Keye-VL-8B and InternVL3.5-8B comparisons. The reward-reasoner ablation replaces R1-Distilled-1.5B with Qwen3-8B.

E3.justification: The main benchmark splits and metrics remain, but GRPO changes from symmetric 0.2 clipping with KL coefficient 0.001 to asymmetric 0.2/0.25 clipping without KL. v2 adds 72B configurations and changes default ablation inference from R1-7B to Qwen3-8B. New protocols include non-thinking general evaluation, compute estimation using 100 examples per dataset, and four human ratings per caption pair instead of one.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analyses of holistic versus query-relevant captions, caption-penalty effectiveness and reward hacking, sequential training and reasoning forgetting, and training/inference compute tradeoffs. Component ablations are redesigned in Tables 2 and 7. The lengthy caption and reasoning case studies from v1 Tables 7–19 are retained as v2 Tables 9–21.

E5.justification: v2 adds aggregation of four annotators' decisions and an inter-annotator agreement estimate, supplementing the existing GPT-human agreement measure (Appendix E.3). This is a localized expansion of reliability reporting; handling of 2–2 voting ties remains unspecified. Neither version reports seed-based benchmark uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced or added. Table 1 reports 47.4% for v1's CRO-only 7B/Qwen3-8B configuration and 53.2% for v2's revised GRPO/VPO configuration; these use different training procedures. v2 adds a 72B/GPT-OSS result of 58.0%. Human win/tie/loss rates change from 60/29/11% to 62/32/6% under the revised annotation design.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the formal caption-penalty reward definition in Equation 3 and changes the VPO objective to separate lower and upper clipping parameters. The underlying GRPO formulation is retained, and neither version develops additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about decoupled perception, reasoning-reward optimization, and retraining-free reasoner upgrades persist. v2 moderates the abstract and conclusion from state-of-the-art performance claims to significant accuracy gains. Inference-time scaling receives greater emphasis, but that capability was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of caption reward hacking, why query-relevant captions optimize better despite weaker initial performance, and small-model reasoning forgetting. Appendix H expands the earlier domain-extension limitation into concrete qualifications about required adaptations, general evaluations excluding the reasoner, automatic thinking-mode selection, and the frozen reasoning LLM.

D1.justification: v2 provides substantially richer training and checkpoint-selection documentation, including evaluation every 50 steps and selection by average benchmark accuracy. It adds the caption-checking prompt, penalty coefficient, training-token estimates, and compute-estimation procedures. These disclosures exceed v1's basic hyperparameters and prompts. The reported code-access link changes from RACRO2 to RAPID.

R1.justification: Section 2 gains a dedicated caption-then-reason discussion, adding earlier pipelines such as those of Tiong, Guo, and Hu. Existing ECSO and OmniCaptioner citations receive substantive treatment. v2 acknowledges prior query-aware captioning and positions its distinction around tentative solutions and outcome-based optimization, revising v1's positioning around query-conditioned, reasoning-aligned representations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten, with RAPID/VPO terminology replacing RACRO/CRO. Generalization and caption evaluation become separate subsections. The appendices gain a contents list and substantial reorganization; the earlier broader-impact and future-work sections disappear, and an LLM-writing disclosure is added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged and rescaled, and the earlier hallucination illustration is replaced by a quantitative perception-strategy comparison. Main tables are restructured, with new general-benchmark, reward-hacking, training, and compute plots. Reward and caption-length plots are separated and expanded. Existing case tables are retained and reflowed within a different document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through direct caption-then-reason comparisons, diagnosis and mitigation of reward hacking, and explicit compute and general-ability analyses (Table 1, Figure 7, Appendices D–E). Fuller implementation details and applicability limitations substantially strengthen the paper's evidential support and transparency. Removing the VisualPRM comparison and introducing inconsistencies in training-order and ablation descriptions temper these gains, but do not outweigh them.
